_status: FROZEN as part of a prior retirement curation on 2026-08-04. These are user questions, intentionally phrased differently from the Base card titles and bodies. The set covers foundational methodology plus every newly curated retirement method; re-confirm before changing an expected ref.

queries.query: Can a deterministic string check decide whether a response means the right thing, or is that the kind of question that needs semantic judgment?
The candidate score rose slightly, but the reviewers disagree a lot. How do I tell whether that improvement is signal rather than evaluator noise?
Our synthetic cases never reproduce what users actually report. What is the disciplined way to turn real incidents into test evidence?
A test scaffold calls its own panel of models and labels outputs locally. Why is that not a valid release verdict?
The evaluator refuses to freeze the baseline. Should we relax the threshold to get a result, or treat that refusal as evidence?
queries.note: Gate refusal is a diagnosis, not permission to lower the gate.

queries.query: A behavior is missing, but how do I first establish whether the system ever receives the facts needed to produce it?
queries.note: Source availability and eligibility before prompt attribution.

queries.query: The same instruction template is reused across many features. If one use is flawed, how should we scope the repair and its regression test?
Our experiment pins a provider and configuration, but production may run something else. Is the experiment still a valid control?
A context value looks correct before cleanup, yet the model behaves as if it never saw it. Where should I inspect?
Repeated runs are either completely clean or completely broken. What should the report show instead of a reassuring small-sample average?
One recurring defect is inflating our failure rate and different quality dimensions have different judge agreement. What has to be measured before trusting the gate?
queries.note: Feature-level agreement, distinct failures, and paired deltas.

queries.query: A quick smoke run proves the code path changed. Why is that still not enough evidence to close a statistical quality claim?
How can a natural-language test actor be graded when it may invent facts, and how do we stop an adversarial probe from poisoning the state it tests?
queries.note: Explicit truth sheet and adversarial-probe isolation.

queries.query: Why might an evaluator call a correct answer fabricated even though the user had already established the fact earlier in the exchange?
A structured grader occasionally returns malformed data. What should the system budget and expose instead of quietly treating the run as unavailable?
queries.note: Worst-case structured output and parse failure.

queries.query: I just wrote a knowledge record, but search does not find it. What is the authoritative way to decide whether the write succeeded?
queries.note: Reference read, not ranked retrieval, confirms persistence.

queries.query: How do we test our own knowledge search without accidentally rewarding queries that merely repeat card wording or stale answers?
A frozen regression test turned red after several changes landed. What must we establish before blaming the newest edit or replacing the snapshot?
queries.note: Attribute a red frozen test before revert or re-freeze.

queries.query: Two observations disagree about one stored fact. Why is choosing either the newest or oldest value automatically unsafe?
An extractor misses an explicit detail when it is buried in a long batch. Besides wording, what operating parameter should we tune?
